title: Few‑shot Memory Footprint Benchmark and Priming Budget Spec
author: Asha Raman
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Few‑shot Memory Footprint Benchmark (FMFB) and the associated Priming Budget Spec. FMFB measures how adding few‑shot examples (priming) affects memory usage, KV cache pressure, batching efficiency, latency SLOs, and generation quality across representative models and hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to produce actionable priming budgets and runtime guardrails that minimize operational cost and regression risk.

Scope
- Applies to text-only autoregressive and chat models used in production (decoder‑only LLMs and chat variants).
- Evaluates both default full‑context priming and compact priming (fewshot compressed templates).
- Runs across three representative hardware classes: GPU-large (A100 40GB), GPU-mid (H100 80GB), and edge/accelerator class (L4/NVIDIA T4 class).
- Integrates quantized and full‑precision model artifacts; measures changes per quant profile.

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
- Derive a per-model priming budget expressed as: max_examples, max_tokens_from_examples, and recommended_template (string).
- For any model+deployment tier, priming must not increase median p95 latency by > 15% or p99 latency by > 25% versus a no‑priming baseline under the target QPS.
- KV cache memory delta from priming should be bounded so that cache eviction rate stays < 5% in steady state for dedicated and private deployments.
- Batch utilization must not drop by > 10 percentage points due to priming-induced sequence length variance.
- Quality: Minimal acceptable change in automated coherence score (see Metrics) is delta >= -0.03 absolute (calibrated per task).

Benchmark design
1) Workload selection - Choose three workload archetypes: instruction completion, multi‑turn chat, and structured data extraction. For each archetype, select 6 canonical prompts representing head/mid/tail frequency.
- For each prompt, create three few‑shot templates: long (6 examples), medium (3 examples), short (1 example). Examples span token lengths 30–220 tokens.
2) Model matrix - Evaluate against the following model variants where available: base fp16, q4_K, q5_0, and int8 (if supported).
- Run on both streaming and non‑streaming generation modes.
3) Load profile - Two traffic profiles per workload: steady (50 RPS) and bursty (peak 400 RPS with 5s bursts). Scale test to saturate target SLOs for each deployment tier.
4) Measurement probes - Capture tokenized lengths, KV cache allocation snapshots, scheduler queue lengths, batch sizes, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput, and generation quality metrics (see metrics).

Metrics (definitions and collection)
- Priming memory delta: peak resident memory attributable to prompt tokens + per‑example KV allocations (bytes). Collected via runtime allocator sampling and process RSS differencing.
- Cache eviction rate: percent of requests experiencing an eviction event within a 1h window.
- Batch utilization: ratio of effective tokens processed per batch to theoretical max for hardware.
- Latency: end‑to‑end request latency excluding client network (p50/p95/p99).
- Quality metrics: task‑specific automatic metrics (BLEU/F1 for extraction, coherence score for open generation — see calibration below), semantic similarity to golden answers (embedding cosine), and hallucination rate estimator via heuristic checks.
- Cost proxy: tokens processed * model_cost_per_token + extra GPU seconds attributable to priming overhead.

Calibration and quality thresholding
- Calibrate coherence score using a 500 sample annotated set per archetype. Coherence score maps human ratings (0–1) to automated heuristics combining log‑prob delta and embedding consistency. Documented calibration artifact stored in internal registry.
- Set per‑service minimal acceptable quality delta based on business criticality: high (delta >= -0.01), medium (delta >= -0.03), low (delta >= -0.06).

Runbook: executing FMFB
Preconditions
1. Select model artifact tags and quant profiles to test.
2. Ensure telemetry ingestion for runtime allocator, batcher, and KV cache deltas is enabled.
3. Provision test dedicated pools or isolated private deployment (shadow).
Procedure
1. Prepare template corpus
   a) Generate tokenized versions for each example and save as JSON lines.
   b) Annotate golden outputs for extraction tasks.
2. Baseline run (no priming)
   - Warmup 10k requests across archetypes.
   - Collect baseline metrics for 30 minutes under steady and bursty profiles.
3. Priming runs
   - Run short, medium, long priming templates sequentially.
   - For each run: execute warmup, then 30m steady profile, 1h burst simulation.
4. Postprocessing
   - Compute deltas against baseline for memory, latency, batch utilization, cache eviction, and quality.
   - Produce per-model CSV report and a summarized Confluence table.
5. Decisioning
   - If any acceptance criteria are violated, mark model+template as "Not Approved" for the deployment tier.
   - If memory but not quality is violated, evaluate compact priming (template compression, example truncation).
   - If latency violated but memory within bounds, surface to serving runtime with suggested batching overrides and autoscaling adjustments.

Compact priming strategies (automated mitigations)
- Example trimming: reduce each example to core tokens using extractor heuristics (retain first and last 12 tokens).
- Example summarization: generate compressed summaries with a 4–8 token anchor plus 8 token paraphrase.
- Template condensation: move metadata outside the token budget into structured tool calls or functioncall metadata where supported.

Configuration table (benchmark harness YAML snippet)
| key | value | notes |
|-----|-------|-------|
| models | ["redwood-rlhf-70b:fp16","redwood-70b:q5_0","open-compat-13b:q4_K"] | artifact tags to evaluate |
| hardware_classes | ["A100-40GB","H100-80GB","L4"] | representative tiers |
| workloads | ["instruction","chat","extraction"] | archetypes |
| priming_templates | ["short","medium","long"] | examples per template |
| steady_rps | 50 | baseline profile |
| burst_profile | {peak:400,burst_duration_s:5} | synthetic bursts |

YAML example (for harness config):
```yaml
harness:
  timeout_seconds: 3600
  concurrency: 32
  collectors:
    - kv_cache_sampler
    - batcher_metrics
    - latency_histogram
  scenarios:
    - name: steady
      rps: 50
      duration_minutes: 30
    - name: bursts
      pattern: poisson
      peak_rps: 400
      duration_minutes: 60
```

Triage playbook (if regression detected)
1. Confirm reproducibility: re-run failing template against isolated replica.
2. Pin model artifact to prior known-good build to test delta.
3. Check quant profile differences; run the same template with fp16 artifact.
4. Inspect KV cache telemetry: high eviction rate -> reduce priming tokens or increase cache size config.
5. Inspect batcher heatmaps: increased variance in seq length -> consider dynamic microbatching or template standardization.
6. If quality regression with quantized artifact: escalate to Applied ML for targeted quant re‑tuning and label a new probe for regression triage.
7. Document RCA and attach CSV artifacts to the FMFB run page.

Ownership and cadence
- Benchmark steward: Applied ML Eval squad (primary: Asha Raman).
- Operational owner for harness and telemetry: Runtime team (secondary: Diego Torres).
- Run cadence: weekly runs for top 5 production models, quarterly for full model matrix.
- Promotion gate: models pass FMFB before being allowed primed templates in production routes.

Outputs and artifacts
- Per-run CSV with metrics per scenario.
- Consolidated Confluence summary table with recommended priming budget (max_examples, max_tokens, template_id).
- JSON policy file to be consumed by Runtime to automatically enforce per-route priming caps (example below).

Policy JSON example (enforced by routing layer):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "redwood-70b:q5_0",
  "priming_budget": {"max_examples": 3, "max_priming_tokens": 512},
  "enforcement": "reject\\n- truncate\\n- warn",
  "quality_anchor": "coherence_calib_v1"
}
```

Notes and considerations
- Edge deployments with strict memory caps should default to compact priming templates and explicit template truncation in the SDK.
- Streaming mode exposes a different cost profile — capture streaming-specific allocation traces as part of FMFB.
- Priming interacts with functioncall routing and tool arguments; for tool‑heavy flows prefer moving examples to metadata where supported.
